intent: Audit every document in the repository so that what is written is current, relevant and navigable, for a human operator and for an agent booting cold. Operator asked for this on 2026-08-30, framed as keeping the codebase clean and tidy and easy for both humans and AI agents to navigate. Scope is the whole documentary surface: 39 files under docs/, the agentic entry points (AGENTS.md and its byte-identical CLAUDE.md copy, README.md), and the EOS governance files under org/. The case for it is not hypothetical: this session alone found and fixed six separate pieces of documentation that were wrong about the running code, listed under evidence.
evidence_this_is_needed: docs/API.md described read-only as enforced per route by requireAuth(), a model the security hotfix replaced long before T-0048 deleted the function. It documented an architecture that had not existed for months.

docs/ENV_REFERENCE.md and docs/SECURITY.md both said 'Reads keep working' under PS_READ_ONLY. That was ASPIRATIONAL, not descriptive: 34 read handlers returned 503. The docs were right about the intent and wrong about the product, which is the most misleading combination.

docs/USER_WALKTHROUGH_GUIDE.md filed Insights under the Main nav group and gave its route as /insights, which does not exist; described a '+ New' button on Personalities that the page deliberately does not have; and carried a screenshot caption admitting the image was 'stale in three ways'.
The guide had NO coverage at all of Composer, Deep Research, Artifacts or the spend console, four surfaces that had shipped.

A QA brief written from a survey of the codebase repeated two errors it inherited: that POST /api/tools returns 410 (it returns 405, via methodNotAllowed) and that the boot line advertises the wrong port (it does not; Next assigns process.env.PORT at bind time). Both were caught only by measuring.

docs/PRODUCT_MAP.md is a blank Genesis template that says of itself 'Until Genesis runs this file is a blank form and every section is draft'. Whether it should exist yet is a decision, not an oversight, but a reader cannot tell that from the file's position in the index.

2026-08-30, and the sharpest evidence yet because it is self-inflicted: spend-summary.ts carried a comment asserting that Composer runs are priced at a conservative DEFAULT_RATE. Nothing wrote their tokens, so the spend console excluded the whole source and showed $0.00. The comment was written during T-0030 and then READ BACK AS EVIDENCE when writing a QA brief, which carried the false claim to a tester as a do-not-file instruction. A wrong comment did not merely fail to help; it actively suppressed the report of a real money-adjacent defect for as long as it stood. See T-0058.
scope: docs/ — 39 markdown files, 28 to 2016 lines. For each: is it TRUE of the code at HEAD, is it still RELEVANT, and is it discoverable from the index. Retire what describes a subsystem that no longer exists (the benchmark subsystem was deleted at 4935ac31; check what still mentions it).

The agentic entry points. AGENTS.md is hard-capped at 40 lines by check-agent-files.mjs and CLAUDE.md must stay byte-identical; the cap exists because AGENTS.md once reached 183 lines, went stale, and agents followed it anyway into CSS variables that did not exist. The question is not whether it is short but whether the 31 lines it spends are the right ones for an agent booting cold.
org/ — CONSTITUTION, START, PLAYBOOKS, TEMPLATES, TESTING, GRAPH_BUILD, QUESTIONS. TASKS.md and STATE.md are DERIVED and must not be hand-edited; check-derived-views.mjs enforces that.
README.md as the front door for a human arriving from GitHub.

The relationship between them. A reader should be able to answer 'where do I look for X' without grep. Today there are at least three overlapping entry points (README, docs/README, REPO_GUIDE) and it is not obvious which is authoritative for what.
acceptance: Every doc is either current, or deleted, or explicitly marked as historical with a date and a reason. A stale document that nobody can tell is stale is worse than a missing one, because it is followed.
No document describes an architecture the code does not have. Spot-checked against source, not against other documents.
One authoritative index, and every document reachable from it in one hop.
AGENTS.md still passes its 40-line cap and CLAUDE.md is still byte-identical.
npm run lint stays green, including check-doc-links and the no-em-dash rule, which has one sanctioned pragma today and should not gain more without a written reason.
proposed_ratchet: The deeper problem is that nothing checks a document against the code it describes. check-doc-links.mjs proves links RESOLVE; it cannot notice that API.md documents a deleted function. Worth considering as part of this task, and worth costing before committing to: a dependency-free check that every `src/...` path and every exported identifier quoted in backticks inside docs/ actually exists. That would have caught API.md's requireAuth reference, the walkthrough guide's /insights route, and the Personalities '+ New' button. It would NOT have caught the aspirational 'Reads keep working', which no mechanical check can reach; that one needs a human reading the sentence against the behaviour. T-0058 sharpens the case for a second, narrower check that would have caught the worst instance: spend-summary.ts names its three sources in prose, and nothing asserts that each named source actually has a writer. Both spend defects found so far (T-0030 research, T-0058 composer) were found by a human reading that one comment, months apart. A test that enumerates the sources the comment claims and asserts a writer exists for each would have caught the second at the first.
notes: Do NOT hand-edit org/TASKS.md or org/STATE.md. They are derived and regenerated by taskops.render_views. Note that `python -m tools.eos task views` regenerates the EOS checkout's own views rather than this repo's, which is filed as friction in EOS_FEEDBACK.md; the working invocation is in the failure message of check-derived-views.mjs.
docs/QA_NOTES.md grew substantially on 2026-08-30 and is current. It is the one document a QA pass must read first, and the audit should protect rather than trim it.
docs/EOS_FEEDBACK.md is append-only by convention and carries a finding about the EOS tooling itself. It is a channel, not a description of the product; audit it for accuracy, not for relevance.
already_done: Three defects from this audit are FIXED at 17c0b662 and should not be re-investigated: API.md said POST /api/tools returns 410 (it returns 405); USER_WALKTHROUGH_GUIDE.md still offered the sepia and light reader themes removed in WO-0005; QA_NOTES.md said toasts auto-dismiss in ~4s, which stopped being true of ERROR toasts at T-0050 and was the dangerous half.

The walkthrough guide was substantially rewritten this round and now covers Composer, Deep Research, Artifacts and the spend console, which it previously did not mention at all. Audit it for accuracy, not for coverage of those four.
scope_correction: The scope written when this task was opened understates the surface and is corrected here. It said 'docs/ - 39 markdown files'. `git ls-files 'docs/*.md'` returns 45: the original count came from a top-level listing and missed docs/adr/README.md, the three docs/genesis/ templates and the two docs/schema/ files. More importantly the REPO holds 110 tracked .md files, and the task named only docs/, org/, README and AGENTS/CLAUDE. Unowned and unaudited by the original scope: OPERATORS_GUIDE.md (184 lines, the human's manual, and orphaned - only the compile manifest mentions it), REBRANDING.md, TRADEMARK.md, ops/runbooks/deploy.md (the file a restore drill is RUN from), the three .github/ templates, branding/ x4, src/kit/PROVENANCE.md, tests/scripts/README.md, and 24 files under data/seed/ which are shipped product content rather than documentation about the product. Real defects were found in four of those areas, so the omission was not harmless.
audit_method: A 205-agent workflow over twelve document groups, each agent required to verify claims against SOURCE and to produce a src path:line for every finding, followed by one adversarial verifier per finding instructed to REFUTE and to default to refuted when it could not independently confirm both halves (that the doc says it, and that the evidence supports it). 191 raw findings, 160 confirmed, 27 refuted, 4 verifiers lost to API safeguard errors unrelated to content. A 14% refute rate is low enough to be worth stating plainly, so two confirmed findings were re-checked by hand before any were acted on: /api/memory's POST/PUT/DELETE really are all bound to a 400 handler, and prebuild-db really compares `< 3` rather than `!== 3`. Both held. The full finding set is exported to scratchpad/t0057-findings.json and the run journal.
premises_the_audit_corrected: I briefed the workflow that docs/COMPILE_REPORT.md had become a de-facto second index because it referenced nearly every orphan. It contains ZERO markdown links; `grep -c '](' ` returns 0 against 32 in docs/README.md. Every apparent link is a bare path in a pipe-table cell of an ancestry manifest. It is a provenance record, and there was nothing to demote.

I briefed that docs/LABORATORY.md advertises a deleted Benchmarks subsystem. It does the opposite: ':20 says "There is no Benchmarks page" and explains why /benchmarks 404s rather than redirecting. The stale claim was in docs/README.md's INDEX ROW for that file. The index contradicted the document it indexes, and I had repeated the index's own error while scouting.

Six of the ten orphans cannot be relocated at all. Their paths come from an external scale matrix (PatterTech_EOS/kernel/SCALE_MATRIX.md) and scripts/tooling/eos-compile.mjs rewrites them on every compile, so a move from this repo is undone from another one. Verified against the matrix directly before deleting anything.
done_so_far: BATCH A, security-adjacent (4f5a4aef). README.md claimed `npm run start` binds 'this machine only'. MEASURED with netstat, not read: it binds 0.0.0.0 AND [::], and Next prints the LAN URL itself. Both start scripts have identical exposure. The same false distinction was repeated in src/proxy.ts's header and in SECURITY.md, which also advised a loopback bind the repo ships no script for. PLATFORM_VISION.md said to treat UI and API as 'same-trust' and CONTRIBUTING.md said 'there is no global API-key wall'; proxy.ts requires a token on every path and fails CLOSED. ops/runbooks/deploy.md gave a restore path no writer produces (wrong directory and wrong filename shape) and said the auth token is minted on first request when it is minted at boot.

BATCH B+C (1b4f9728). The four live present-tense references to requireAuth, deleted in T-0048 - the worst being TESTING.md, which told you to mirror a mock pattern the T-0049 check now FAILS THE BUILD for. Plus eleven mechanical errors: schema_version 30 vs 34 (in the sentence that warns against restating version numbers in prose), 2,279 tests vs 3,214, `npm run discover-agents` vs `discover-hermes`, isChReadOnly, AccentColor's file, the LABORATORY index row, two schema constants that never existed, a missing ADR-0009 row, the PR template's derived-file instruction and its two 404ing links, OPERATORS_GUIDE dropping `secrets` from always_human, and a stale requireAuth comment in src/app/api/config/route.ts.

BATCH NAV (2207d50b). docs/ now has ZERO orphans, measured, down from ten: four missing product rows plus a Governance (EOS) section that says why those six cannot move. docs/PATTERSTAGE.md deleted after measuring that all 14 documents it linked to already appear in the index; its unique paragraph moved to REPO_GUIDE.md and six inbound links redirected. The hand-sync cluster closed: three docs told contributors to keep two DERIVED files in sync, which is the practice that caused the drift the derivation removed.

BATCH FINAL (3959bd43 and follow-up). Ten agents with exclusive per-file ownership fixed the remaining confirmed findings, ten more verified against source: 200 fixed, 13 already done, 2 rejected as not-real on re-check. 200 exceeds the 160 confirmed because agents were told to fix adjacent errors they could prove. LOCKBOOK.md was the most consequential: six ratchets recorded as UNMET are demonstrably MET, each verified against the migration that satisfies it. The walkthrough guide's sidebar was documented as five sections with Laboratory missing entirely; Cancel claimed a process kill that exists nowhere in its path; chat was documented as localStorage when it has been server-side since migration 013.
remaining: Roughly 128 of the 160 confirmed findings are unfixed, concentrated in USER_WALKTHROUGH_GUIDE.md (39 raw), API.md (11), TESTING.md (10), README.md (8), LOCKBOOK.md (8), CONTRIBUTING.md (7) and MIGRATION.md (7). Work them by document rather than by severity: the audit showed defects cluster inside a file, so a reader is either well served by a document or repeatedly misled by it. LOCKBOOK.md is matrix-addressed, so check whether a fix belongs upstream in the EOS pack before editing it here.
ratchet_costed: Prototyped and MEASURED, with an honest false-positive rate rather than a flattering one. A backticked-path checker over 59 live documents finds 7 unresolved references out of 379. Only about 3 are real: SYSTEM-CRON's path is inside $HERMES_HOME and not this repo, QUESTIONS.md correctly says the v2 recompile RETIRES org/QUEUE.md, and GRAPH_BUILD's docs/PARTITION.md is an instruction to create a file rather than a claim that it exists. An identifier checker over 392 backticked identifiers finds 5 absent, of which 2 are real (isChReadOnly, a Personalities typo) and one - REPO_GUIDE's 'No withApiRoute HOF' - names a pattern the repo DELIBERATELY does not have. That is the design constraint: a document correctly recording an ABSENCE is indistinguishable, to any mechanical check, from one wrongly claiming a presence. A useful ratchet therefore needs a negation-context escape with a written reason, in the WG-WEB-013 pragma style. It would also have missed requireAuth entirely, because a stale COMMENT in src/app/api/config/route.ts kept the identifier alive in the haystack. Worth building, but as a net with a documented catch rate, not as a proof.
closing_verification: Acceptance checked item by item rather than asserted. (1) Zero orphans in docs/, measured, down from ten. (2) AGENTS.md within its 40-line cap and CLAUDE.md byte-identical, per check-agent-files. (3) npm run lint green, including check-doc-links and the no-em-dash rule, which gained no new pragma. (4) Full gate: lint 0, tsc 0, 3214 tests / 382 suites, knip 0, canary 0, build 0. (5) Both mechanical scanners re-run: every real hit is fixed and the survivors are the documented false-positive classes (external $HERMES_HOME paths, deliberate absences such as REPO_GUIDE's 'No withApiRoute HOF', historical mentions, and two Jest config keys the scanner's haystack does not walk). (6) The eight files nobody had audited (REBRANDING, TRADEMARK, branding/ x4, tests/scripts/README, data/seed/README) read in full and found clean; their three apparently-broken paths resolve correctly relative to data/seed/, and an apparently-stale hex colour was a URL fragment my own regex mis-parsed.
found_beyond_documentation: eos-compile.mjs was a silent no-op reporting success. Left deliberately unrepaired because repairing the parse regenerates 32 files from sibling-repo templates and overwrites hand-edited governance; it now exits 1 on a zero-row matrix instead. Filed in EOS_FEEDBACK.md.

task-record.schema.json is violated by 26 of 58 records because additionalProperties:false forbids the invariants/rollback/verification/deferred keys the practice depends on, and policy.json demands artefacts the schema leaves nowhere legal. Three unambiguous violations fixed, all mine from this session; the divergence reported rather than resolved. Filed in EOS_FEEDBACK.md.
Product defects found by checking docs against code, filed as T-0059: the Insights 'Active days' tile states a number it does not measure, and the range switch governs less than it appears to.
